questions.question: CPGM 7356.002A explicitly excludes which of the following categories of product from its coverage?

options.A: Sterile bulk, large volume parenterals (LVP) and small volume parenterals
options.B: Products regulated by CBER, and veterinary drug products
options.C: Ophthalmic and otic dosage forms, small volume parenterals (SVP), and biotherapeutic drug products
options.D: All sterile products made by sterile filtration followed by aseptic filling, or by terminal sterilization

questions.explanation: The program covers all sterile drug products, including sterile bulk, ophthalmic, otic, SVP and LVP, and both terminally sterilized and aseptically processed products; only products regulated by CBER and veterinary drug products are excluded.

questions.question: When an investigator cites deficiencies, what is the status of the 2004 Aseptic Processing Guidance?

options.A: The guidance is mandatory, and deficiencies can be cited directly on guidance provisions as the sole basis
options.B: The guidance applies only to foreign firms; deficiencies at domestic firms may not cite it, and no alternative approaches are allowed
options.C: Following the guidance exempts the firm from also complying with 21 CFR 210 and 211
options.D: The guidance is not binding; the basis for deficiencies is 21 CFR 210/211, and alternative approaches may be used

questions.explanation: The guidance represents FDA's current thinking, does not establish mandatory requirements, and should not be used as the basis for citing deficiencies; the basis is the CGMP regulations, 21 CFR 210 and 211, and a firm may use alternative approaches as long as it complies with the regulations.

questions.question: What does "sterile bulk" in the footnote of this program refer to?

options.A: Sterile APIs
options.B: Filled, sterile finished-product batches that have not yet been packaged and labeled
options.C: Large quantities of unpartitioned formulated solution awaiting terminal sterilization
options.D: Sterile diluents, rinsing solutions and irrigation solutions dispensed in large containers

questions.explanation: The footnote explicitly states that sterile bulk means sterile APIs, so one of the objectives is to inspect manufacturers of sterile APIs as well as sterile finished dosage forms; none of the other options is the definition used in this program.

questions.question: A firm makes an injectable with a labeled volume of less than 100 mL by terminal sterilization. Which profile class should it be assigned in FACTS?

options.A: LVP, because all injectables are reported under this class
options.B: SVS, because it is a small volume parenteral made by sterile filtration and aseptic processing
options.C: SVT, because it is a terminally sterilized small volume parenteral
options.D: SVL, because it is a small volume parenteral that is sterile filtered, aseptically filled and lyophilized

questions.explanation: SVT is a terminally sterilized small volume parenteral labeled at less than 100 mL; SVS is filtered and aseptically processed, SVL additionally involves lyophilization, and LVP is a large volume parenteral labeled at more than 100 mL.

questions.question: While fully inspecting one system, an investigator follows up on some items of another system to obtain evidence. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The follow-up counts as full coverage of the second system and should be reported in FACTS as full coverage
options.B: The follow-up does not constitute full coverage of the second system, and does not oblige the investigator to inspect it fully afterwards
options.C: The second system must be changed to a full inspection item and the whole inspection plan redrawn
options.D: Follow-up is limited to the quality system, and other systems may not be followed up across each other, to preserve the independence of the inspection

questions.explanation: The program explains that following up on another system in order to fully document findings is not full coverage of that system, cannot be reported as such in FACTS, and does not oblige the investigator to inspect that system fully.
questions.reference: FDA CPGM 7356.002A Section 2.2 A (1) Inspection of Systems

questions.question: Which comparison of the overkill and bioburden-based approaches to terminal sterilization is correct?

options.A: Overkill is commonly used for heat-stable materials and provides a high sterility assurance regardless of the actual number and resistance of the bioburden, but gives the product a greater heat/exposure load
options.B: Overkill requires first studying the number and resistance of microorganisms in the product to design the cycle, and routinely monitors the bioburden of every batch
options.C: The bioburden-based approach is suited to heat-stable materials, gives the product more heat, and does not require tracking of bioburden data
options.D: Both must rely on bioburden monitoring of every batch, differing only in frequency and sampling location

questions.explanation: Overkill is used for heat-stable materials and is designed to give sufficient sterility assurance regardless of the amount and resistance of the bioburden, at the cost of higher heat input; the bioburden-based approach requires studying the number and resistance of microorganisms and continuous monitoring.

questions.question: According to this program, which comparison of aseptic processing and terminal sterilization is correct?

options.A: The contamination risks are comparable, differing only in the type of sterilization equipment and the frequency of validation
options.B: Aseptic processing has fewer variables, because all components are already sterilized before filling
options.C: Aseptic processing carries a higher risk of microbial contamination and involves more variables, as the product and container are sterilized separately and then combined
options.D: Terminal sterilization carries a higher risk, because the product is sterilized only in its final container, where bioburden is harder to control

questions.explanation: The program states that aseptic processing carries a higher contamination risk than terminal sterilization and has more variables, as any manual or mechanical manipulation can cause contamination; if the product and container closure system can withstand terminal sterilization, it should be used.

questions.question: A firm has several aseptic filling lines. According to this program, which one should be given priority coverage during the inspection?

options.A: The filling line with the largest output and the most batches, because it represents the scale of overall operations
options.B: The new filling line most recently validated, because its data are the most complete and easiest to review
options.C: The filling line that uses an isolator, because its design is the most complex and the hardest to review
options.D: The filling line with the most manual manipulation in the Class 100 (ISO 5) area

questions.explanation: The program calls for priority coverage of the systems and areas with the highest contamination risk, such as the filling line with the most manual manipulation in the Class 100 (ISO 5) area; for terminally sterilized products, the choice is a heat-sensitive product that requires a product-specific bioburden-based cycle.

questions.question: According to this program, what is the coverage requirement for a Full Inspection?

options.A: At least two systems, one of which is the quality system, with the others left to the investigator's judgment
options.B: At least four systems, which must include the quality system and should include Facilities & Equipment and Production
options.C: All six systems must be covered, with none omitted, to ensure a complete and comprehensive assessment
options.D: At least three systems, which must include both the Laboratory and Materials systems, inspected together

questions.explanation: A Full Inspection normally covers at least four systems, one of which must be the quality system; the program further requires inclusion of Facilities & Equipment and Production, because these two are critical to the sterility assurance of the finished product.

questions.question: To qualify for an Abbreviated Inspection, which compliance record condition must the firm meet?

options.A: The last three inspections were all VAI, and any recalls were Class 2 or lower
options.B: The most recent inspection was OAI, but a written improvement plan has been submitted and initial corrections completed
options.C: Two consecutive NAI inspections (or at most one VAI), and no Class 1 recalls
options.D: No FDA inspection in the past five years, and all products are terminally sterilized large volume parenterals

questions.explanation: The program gives a satisfactory record as two consecutive NAI inspections, or at most one VAI, with no Class 1 recalls; it also requires no sterility failures of distributed batches and a formal risk management plan.

questions.question: This program states that the inspection of the quality system has two phases. What is the focus of the second phase?

options.A: Confirming that the quality unit has approved all procedures, and assessing whether these procedures are suitable for use in production
options.B: Checking the facility validation reports to confirm that the design specifications meet the cleanroom grade
options.C: Observing operators on the production line to assess whether aseptic technique and gowning procedures are carried out
options.D: Evaluating the data collected by the firm to identify potential quality problems, and reviewing how the firm uses data to judge the state of control

questions.explanation: The first phase assesses whether the quality unit fulfills its responsibility to approve procedures and ensure they are suitable; the second phase evaluates the data collected by the firm to identify potential quality problems, and reviews how the firm uses data to judge the state of control of manufacturing and facilities.

questions.question: In the inspection of the quality system, which category of deviation investigation should be reviewed regardless of the final disposition?

options.A: All initial positive sterility tests, endotoxin failures and media fill failures
options.B: Only sterility test failures finally judged OOS and leading to rejection of the whole batch
options.C: Only abnormal finished-product appearance for which an investigation was started after a complaint or Field Alert report
options.D: Only sterilization process failures that occurred during validation and were followed up after revalidation was complete

questions.explanation: The program specifically lists review of all initial positive sterility tests, endotoxin failures and media fill failures, regardless of the final disposition; it also includes sterilization/depyrogenation failures during validation or revalidation, and environmental and personnel monitoring results that exceed alert or action limits.

questions.question: According to this program, to what degree should validation of the decontamination of isolator interior surfaces demonstrate a reduction of the biological indicator (BI)?

options.A: A 3-log reduction, because the decontaminating agent only needs to deal with ordinary surface contamination
options.B: A 6-log reduction, with near-infrared or chemical indicators used to find the worst-case locations
options.C: A 12-log reduction, because decontamination must reach the same level as steam sterilization
options.D: No log reduction needs to be specified, as long as environmental monitoring after decontamination shows no colonies

questions.explanation: Validation of decontamination of isolator interior surfaces should show a 6-log reduction of the BI; decontaminating agents such as VHP can sterilize surfaces but lack the penetrating power of steam, so worst-case locations must be identified for placing BIs.

questions.question: A filling line is billed as a RABS, but during filling the doors are frequently opened for routine interventions. How should this be viewed under this program?

options.A: It is still an open RABS, as long as disinfection is performed after each opening of the door
options.B: It is a special case of closed RABS, because the doors are opened only in planned situations
options.C: It is not considered a RABS, because it no longer restricts access to the critical area
options.D: It is equivalent to an isolator, because both use glove ports and can separate operators

questions.explanation: The doors of a closed RABS are never opened during operation; an open RABS is opened only in a few predefined circumstances. If the doors are opened routinely during filling, access to the critical area is no longer restricted, so it is not considered a RABS.

questions.question: A firm is carrying out construction near an aseptic cleanroom and wants to resume production once it is finished. What should the investigator confirm?

options.A: The firm confirmed acceptable environmental control through appropriate measures (such as environmental monitoring and media fill) before resuming production
options.B: As long as the construction contractor provides a completion certificate, production can resume directly with no additional evaluation
options.C: Only the air velocity of the HEPA filters needs to be recalibrated, with no further environmental monitoring or media fill
options.D: The construction was limited to non-critical areas, so microbial control is not affected at all and no evaluation is needed

questions.explanation: Moving walls and construction can release microorganisms such as fungal spores, so the program calls for confirming that, before resuming production, the firm used appropriate measures such as environmental monitoring and media fill to return the facility to an acceptable state of environmental control.

questions.question: A firm buys ready-to-sterilize rubber stoppers and does not run pyrogen/endotoxin tests on each incoming lot. According to this program, how should the firm ensure their reliability?

options.A: Rely entirely on the certificate issued by the supplier, with no separate verification and no periodic testing
options.B: Wash and depyrogenate them in-house instead, because purchased stoppers cannot be pyrogen-free
options.C: Establish the reliability of the supplier's test results through supplier qualification, and test periodically thereafter
options.D: Audit the supplier site once a year only, with no testing of the incoming product at all

questions.explanation: The program notes that the firm remains responsible for the quality of the stoppers; if pyrogen/endotoxin testing is not performed on each incoming lot, the reliability of the supplier's test results must be established through supplier qualification, with periodic testing, and the specification should state the pyrogen requirement.
questions.reference: FDA CPGM 7356.002A Section 3.7 (3) Pre-washed / Ready to Sterilize Closures

questions.question: According to this program, how should container closure integrity (CCI) be demonstrated?

options.A: Only once at the marketing application stage, with no need to evaluate it again or include it in the stability program
options.B: Solely by the sterility test result of each finished batch, with no other study data needed
options.C: As long as dimensions are confirmed to meet specification on receipt, integrity is considered demonstrated, and no other testing is needed
options.D: Demonstrated during validation and continued in the stability program, as a replacement for sterility testing

questions.explanation: The program calls for container closure integrity to be demonstrated during validation and in the stability program throughout shelf life (which can replace sterility testing), and for confirming that the test adequately simulates the stresses of sterilization, handling and storage, and that its sensitivity is clearly defined.
questions.reference: FDA CPGM 7356.002A Section 3.7 (6) Container / Closure Integrity

questions.question: According to this program, which statement about the frequency and coverage of media fills for aseptic processing is correct?

options.A: Once a year for each production line, with the day shift taken to represent the other shifts
options.B: Every six months for each line; and, except for isolators, at least once per shift for each line
options.C: Once before the first launch of each new product, and repeated afterwards depending on deviations
options.D: Once a quarter, and once per shift whether or not the process uses an isolator

questions.explanation: The program calls for a media fill every six months for each processing line, covering the activities and interventions of all shifts; except for isolator operations, at least once per shift per line, so multi-shift production may need more than one media fill within 6 months.
questions.reference: FDA CPGM 7356.002A Section 3.8 (1) Media fills or process simulations

questions.question: If rubber stoppers are depyrogenated by dilution through repeated WFI rinses, what should the validation demonstrate?

options.A: A successful 3-log reduction in bacterial endotoxin
options.B: A successful 6-log reduction in bacterial endotoxin
options.C: A successful 12-log reduction in microbial load (bioburden)
options.D: No detectable particles, and endotoxin reduced to zero

questions.explanation: The program states that depyrogenation can be achieved by dilution through repeated WFI rinses, and its validation should demonstrate a successful 3-log reduction in bacterial endotoxin; a 6-log reduction is the requirement for BI decontamination of isolators and is unrelated here.
questions.reference: FDA CPGM 7356.002A Section 3.8 (3) Sterilization and depyrogenation of containers, closures and processing equipment

questions.question: What does this program provide regarding parametric release of terminally sterilized products?

options.A: It applies to all terminally sterilized products, including those sterilized by irradiation or ethylene oxide, with no separate filing required
options.B: Any product with good environmental monitoring data may be released directly without a sterility test
options.C: It can be used for products made by aseptic processing with sterile filtration, provided the firm's quality unit approves it
options.D: It is limited to products terminally sterilized by heat, and must be specified in the application and approved

questions.explanation: Parametric release replaces the sterility test with critical data from a sterilization process shown to be in control; it is permitted only for products terminally sterilized by heat, must be specified as a release method in the appropriate application, and the product must have an approved application.

questions.question: Sterile finished products are sometimes stored unlabeled for a period after filling. What does this program require?

options.A: Unlabeled finished product may not be stored; labeling must be completed on the day of filling, with no exceptions
options.B: The firm must have adequate controls to ensure that unlabeled product can be correctly identified at all times
options.C: Only a manual check of the product name at labeling is needed, with no identification or control during storage
options.D: Unlabeled finished product is always treated as nonconforming product and must be reported to the regulatory authority in writing

questions.explanation: The program explains that it is not unusual for filled containers to be stored unlabeled, but the firm must have adequate controls to ensure that unlabeled product can be correctly identified at all times; the time that refrigerated product spends warming up before labeling should also be tracked.

questions.question: What key point does this program make about sterility testing?

options.A: Increasing the number of samples greatly raises the probability of detecting low-level contamination, so the more samples the better
options.B: Doubling the incubation time is enough to detect contamination at any level, regardless of the number of samples
options.C: Increasing the number of samples or tests does not appreciably raise the probability of detecting very low-level contamination
options.D: The sensitivity of the sterility test is sufficient, so it can replace controls such as environmental monitoring and process validation

questions.explanation: The sterility test has limited sensitivity for detecting batch contamination; if the contamination level is very low, more samples or more tests do not greatly raise the probability of detection, so any positive result is a serious event that requires a thorough investigation.
questions.reference: FDA CPGM 7356.002A Section 3.10 Laboratory Control System

questions.question: A batch has an initial positive sterility test result, and the firm wants to invalidate it. According to this program, under what circumstances is this permitted?

options.A: There is clear documented evidence that the microbial growth was unequivocally caused by laboratory error
options.B: The retest result is negative, so the initial positive is presumed to be a chance event and is invalidated
options.C: The head of the quality unit agrees and signs, and the batch has gone through final sterilization
options.D: The isolated microorganism is a common environmental organism, so accidental contamination at sampling is presumed

questions.explanation: The program requires that an initial positive can be invalidated only when there is clear documented evidence that the microbial growth was unequivocally caused by laboratory error; a negative retest or a presumption that the organism is environmental is not sufficient to invalidate it.
questions.reference: FDA CPGM 7356.002A Section 3.10 Laboratory Control System

questions.question: What does this program say about the use and evaluation of disinfectants?

options.A: A single highly effective disinfectant is enough to deal with all types of microorganisms
options.B: Disinfectant efficacy testing need only be done on laboratory glass slides, without simulating actual surface materials
options.C: The expiry period of a disinfectant does not need to be supported by data and can follow the supplier's labeling
options.D: Most disinfectants are not effective against all microorganisms, so a firm should generally use more than one

questions.explanation: Disinfectants have limitations, and most are not effective against all microorganisms, so more than one should generally be used; efficacy studies should use the same disinfectants and contact times as in production, with coupons of materials representative of production surfaces.
questions.reference: FDA CPGM 7356.002A Section 3.10 Laboratory Control System

questions.question: When an investigator collects finished-product samples for sterility and endotoxin testing, how many sample units does this program recommend?

options.A: 20 units for the sterility test; 48 units for the endotoxin test
options.B: 48 units for the sterility test; 20 units for the endotoxin test
options.C: 100 units for the sterility test; 48 units for the endotoxin test
options.D: 20 units each for the sterility and endotoxin tests, 40 in total

questions.explanation: The program specifies collecting 48 units of finished product for sterility testing and 20 units for endotoxin testing; the option with 20 for sterility and 48 for endotoxin swaps the two numbers, and the other options are not in the program.

questions.question: When FDA laboratories test for sterility, bacterial endotoxin and particulates, which compendial chapters should each be based on, according to this program?

options.A: Sterility USP <71>, endotoxin USP <85>, particulates USP <78>, together with the SAM
options.B: Sterility USP <85>, endotoxin USP <71>, particulates USP <78>, together with the SAM
options.C: Sterility USP <71>, endotoxin USP <78>, particulates USP <85>, together with the IOM
options.D: All three based only on the SAM, without citing the USP, to keep methods consistent across FDA laboratories

questions.explanation: Sterility testing is based on USP <71> and the Sterility Analytical Manual (SAM), bacterial endotoxin on USP <85> and the SAM, and particulates on USP <78>; the SAM supplements the USP, with the aim of standardizing microbiological testing across FDA laboratories.
questions.reference: FDA CPGM 7356.002A Part IV Section 4.2 Analysis

questions.question: Under what circumstances should the District Office recommend regulatory action?

options.A: Immediately upon finding any single CGMP deficiency during an inspection
options.B: Only after a violative physical sample has been collected and the result confirmed by the laboratory
options.C: When the firm is judged not to be in a state of control, and management is unwilling or unable to correct this within an appropriate time
options.D: Only after a report is received that a sterile injectable has already caused patient harm

questions.explanation: When the firm is judged not to be in a state of control and management is unwilling or unable to take corrective action within an appropriate time, the District Office should recommend regulatory action; whether a sample was collected is not a threshold.

questions.question: If a CGMP deficiency poses only minimal risk relative to the intended use of the drug, what is the main approach this program recommends?

options.A: File for an injunction or seizure directly, to keep the product off the market as quickly as possible
options.B: Ask the firm to improve only verbally, with no written record or follow-up
options.C: Require a full recall of all of the firm's marketed products and a suspension of all manufacturing activity
options.D: Rely mainly on voluntary correction by the firm, require written commitments with completion timelines, and have the District Office track progress

questions.explanation: When the risk is minimal, the main action is usually voluntary correction by the firm; the District Office should require all commitments to be made in writing with completion timelines, judge whether the timelines are reasonable, and follow up on progress. Injunction, seizure or recall are chosen when, for example, contaminated sterile injectables are found.

questions.topic: Role of physical samples in regulatory action
questions.question: What is this program's position on the relationship between physical samples and regulatory action?

options.A: Without a violative physical sample, no regulatory or administrative action can be taken against the firm
options.B: Regulatory action is independent of whether a violative physical sample was collected, as long as the deficiencies are well documented
options.C: Charges under CGMP can be brought only when physical sample testing fails
options.D: When physical sample testing is acceptable, the firm is exempt from regulatory action for CGMP deficiencies

questions.explanation: The program explains that regulatory action is independent of the collection of violative physical samples; the absence of a violative sample is no obstacle, and an acceptable sample does not prevent action under CGMP, provided the CGMP deficiencies are well documented.

questions.question: Which set of topics does Attachment A, "Inspections: Points to Consider", of this program cover?

options.A: Only terminal sterilization and packaging labeling, covering inspection questions on steam sterilizers and labeling machines
options.B: Only the laboratory and water systems, covering inspection of LAL, sterility testing and the WFI loop
options.C: Moist heat sterilization, dry heat sterilization/depyrogenation, aseptic filling, lyophilization, isolators, environmental monitoring and biological indicators
options.D: The quality, materials and packaging systems, covering deviation investigations, supplier qualification and labeling control

questions.explanation: Attachment A is a list of questions to assist inspections, covering moist heat sterilization, dry heat sterilization/depyrogenation, aseptic filling, lyophilization, isolators, environmental monitoring and biological indicators; the answers need not be included in the EIR unless relevant.
